source.author: verg
source.text: Procul Ornytus armis ignotis et equo venator Iapyge fertur, cui pellis latos umeros erepta iuvenco pugnatori operit, caput ingens oris hiatus et malae texere lupi cum dentibus albis, agrestisque manus armat sparus; ipse catervis vertitur in mediis et toto vertice supra est.
source.text_original: Procul Ornytus armis / ignotis et equo venator Iapyge fertur, / cui pellis latos umeros erepta iuvenco / pugnatori operit, caput ingens oris hiatus / et malae texere lupi cum dentibus albis, / agrestisque manus armat sparus; ipse catervis / vertitur in mediis et toto vertice supra est.
source.text_english: Far off, Ornytus is borne along in unfamiliar armor and on a Iapygian hunting horse, the skin of a bull calf stripped from a fighting steer covers his broad shoulders, a huge head, the gape of the mouth, and the jaws of a wolf with white teeth conceal it; and a rustic spear arms his hands. He himself turns amid the ranks and stands above them all by a whole head.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: sed neque bella videt Graias neque monstra per urbes ulla: Cleonaeo iam tempora clusus hiatu Alcides; olim Lernae defensus ab angue Areas, et ambobus iam cornua fracta iuvencis.
reuse.text_original: sed neque bella videt Graias neque monstra per urbes / ulla: Cleonaeo iam tempora clusus hiatu / Alcides; olim Lernae defensus ab angue / Areas, et ambobus iam cornua fracta iuvencis.
reuse.text_english: but he sees neither wars among the Greeks nor any monsters through the cities: Alcides is now shut in by the Cleonaean chasm; long ago Arcadia was defended by the serpent of Lerna, and now the horns of both bulls have been broken.
